title: अर्थमन्त्री वाग्लेलाई पूर्वपरराष्ट्रमन्त्री ज्ञवालीको जवाफ- नेपालमा कहिल्यै ‘भारत विरोधी राष्ट्रवादको युग’ थिएन
content:
No ads found for this position काठमाडौं । नेकपा एमालेका नेता प्रदीप ज्ञवालीले अर्थमन्त्री स्वर्णिम वाग्लेको अभिव्यक्तिप्रति आपत्ति जनाएका छन्। नयाँदिल्लीमा आयोजित एनडीटीभी वर्ल्ड समिट २०२६ मा बोल्दै अर्थमन्त्री वाग्लेले नेपालमा भारतविरोधी भावनासँग जोडिएको राष्ट्रवादको युग सकिएको बताएका थिए। उनले भनेका थिए, ‘नेपालमा कुनै समय राष्ट्रवादलाई भारतविरोधी भावनासँग जोडेर हेर्ने गरिन्थ्यो । तर, त्यो युग अब सकिएको छ।’ उनले अर्थमन्त्री वाग्लेलाई कुन युगको कुरा गरेको ? भन्दै सोधेका छन्। पूर्वपराष्ट्रमन्त्री समेत रहेका ज्ञवालीले वाग्लेको यो अभिव्यक्ति गैर-कूटनीतिक, असान्दर्भिक र नेपालको स्वाभिमान एवं हितमा आँच पुर्‍याउने खालको बताएको टिप्पणी गरेका छन्। नेपालमा कहिल्यै ‘भारत विरोधी राष्ट्रवादको युग’ नभएको उनको जवाफ छ। ज्ञवालीको भनाइ जस्ताको त्यस्तै, अर्थमन्त्री डा. स्वर्णिम वाग्लेले नयाँ दिल्लीमा ‘नेपालमा भारत विरोधी राष्ट्रवादको युग सकियो’ भनेर दिएको अभिव्यक्ति गैर–कूटनीतिक, असान्दर्भिक र नेपालको स्वाभिमान एवं हितमा आँच पुर्‍याउने खालको छ । विदेशी भूमि कुनै पनि सरकारी पदाधिकारीका लागि आफ्नो मुलुकको राजनीतिका आन्तरिक मतभिन्नताहरूबारे बोल्ने थलो होइन । नेपालमा कहिल्यै ‘भारत विरोधी राष्ट्रवादको युग’ थिएन । नेपालले जहिल्यै सार्वभौम समानता र पारस्परिक हित एवं सम्मानमा उभिएको मित्रतापूर्ण सम्बन्ध चाह्यो र आज पनि त्यही चाहन्छ । कुनै व्यक्ति या समूह विशेषले राख्ने दृष्टिकोण आफैमा कुनै ‘युग’ होइन । त्यसले समग्र राष्ट्रको प्रतिनिधित्व पनि गर्दैन । अर्थमन्त्रीले कुन ‘युग’ को कुरा गर्नुभएको हो ? नेपाल र भारतका बिचमा कतिपय समस्या छन् । सीमा समस्या, सुरक्षा छाताको आभास दिने १९५० को सम्धीका कतिपय प्रावधान, अनुदार वाणिज्य नीतिका कारण नेपाली उत्पादनहरूले भारतीय बजारमा प्रवेश पाउन व्यहोर्नु पर्ने झन्झट, बढ्दो व्यापार घाटा, सीमामा बनाइएका एकतर्फी बाँधका कारण बर्सेनि हुने नेपाली भूमि डुबान, नेपालले स्वाभाविकै रूपमा पाउनु पर्ने वैकल्पिक हवाई प्रवेश मार्गमा गरिएको आनाकानी आदि । घनिष्ट छिमेकी मित्रसँग यी विषयमा खुलस्त कुरा हुनु आवश्यक छ । समस्यालाई गुन्द्रीमुनि लुकाएर सम्बन्ध बलियो हुँदैन । यी विषयहरू उठाउनु कुनै देश विशेषको विरोध होइन । यो नेपालको राष्ट्रिय हितको प्रश्न हो । हरेक सरकारको दायित्व यस राष्ट्रिय हितको रक्षा गर्नु हो । समाधानको एक मात्र बाटो यी विषयमा बलियो राष्ट्रिय एकता र सहमति निर्माण हो । त्यसको बलमा हुने गम्भीर कूटनीतिक पहल हो । यथार्थलाई ढाकछोप गरेर लिइने तुष्टिकरणको नीतिले राष्ट्रिय हित र स्वाभिमानलाई बलियो बनाउँदैन, बरु तिनमा आँच पुर्‍याउँछ । Kathmandu. CPN-UML leader Pradeep Gyawali has objected to the statement made by Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle. Speaking at the NDTV World Summit 2026 held in New Delhi, Finance Minister Wagle said that the era of nationalism linked to anti-India sentiment in Nepal is over. He had said, 'In Nepal, nationalism was once seen as linked to anti-India sentiment. But that era is over now.' He asked Finance Minister Wagle what era he was talking about. Gyawali, who is also a former foreign minister, has commented that Wagle's statement is undiplomatic, irrelevant, and damaging to Nepal's self-respect and interests. His answer is that there has never been an 'era of anti-India nationalism' in Nepal. Gyawali's statement is as follows, Finance Minister Dr. Swarnim Wagle's statement in New Delhi that 'the era of anti-India nationalism in Nepal is over' is undiplomatic, irrelevant and detrimental to Nepal's self-respect and interests. Foreign soil is not the place for any government official to discuss the internal political differences of their country. There was never an 'era of anti-India nationalism' in Nepal. Nepal has always wanted and still wants friendly relations based on sovereign equality and mutual benefit and respect. The view held by any particular individual or group is not an 'era' in itself. Nor does it represent the nation as a whole. What 'era' is the Finance Minister talking about? There are several problems between Nepal and India. The border issue, some provisions of the 1950 treaty that give the impression of a security umbrella, the hassle that Nepali products have to face to enter the Indian market due to the liberal trade policy, the increasing trade deficit, the annual flooding of Nepali land due to the one-way dams built on the border, the reluctance to provide Nepal with an alternative air entry route that is natural to it, etc. It is important to have open discussions about these issues with close neighbors and friends. Hiding problems under the rug will not strengthen relationships. Raising these issues is not against any particular country. This is a question of Nepal's national interest. It is the responsibility of every government to protect this national interest. The only way to find a solution is to build strong national unity and consensus on these issues, backed by serious diplomatic initiatives. A policy of appeasement that covers up the reality does not strengthen national interests and self-respect, but rather undermines them.

नेपाल र भारतका बिचमा कतिपय समस्या छन् । सीमा समस्या, सुरक्षा छाताको आभास दिने १९५० को सम्धीका कतिपय प्रावधान, अनुदार वाणिज्य नीतिका कारण नेपाली उत्पादनहरूले भारतीय बजारमा प्रवेश पाउन व्यहोर्नु पर्ने झन्झट, बढ्दो व्यापार घाटा, सीमामा बनाइएका एकतर्फी बाँधका कारण बर्सेनि हुने नेपाली भूमि डुबान, नेपालले स्वाभाविकै रूपमा पाउनु पर्ने वैकल्पिक हवाई प्रवेश मार्गमा गरिएको आनाकानी आदि । घनिष्ट छिमेकी मित्रसँग यी विषयमा खुलस्त कुरा हुनु आवश्यक छ । समस्यालाई गुन्द्रीमुनि लुकाएर सम्बन्ध बलियो हुँदैन । यी विषयहरू उठाउनु कुनै देश विशेषको विरोध होइन । यो नेपालको राष्ट्रिय हितको प्रश्न हो । हरेक सरकारको दायित्व यस राष्ट्रिय हितको रक्षा गर्नु हो । समाधानको एक मात्र बाटो यी विषयमा बलियो राष्ट्रिय एकता र सहमति निर्माण हो । त्यसको बलमा हुने गम्भीर कूटनीतिक पहल हो । यथार्थलाई ढाकछोप गरेर लिइने तुष्टिकरणको नीतिले राष्ट्रिय हित र स्वाभिमानलाई बलियो बनाउँदैन, बरु तिनमा आँच पुर्‍याउँछ । Kathmandu. CPN-UML leader Pradeep Gyawali has objected to the statement made by Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle. Speaking at the NDTV World Summit 2026 held in New Delhi, Finance Minister Wagle said that the era of nationalism linked to anti-India sentiment in Nepal is over. He had said, 'In Nepal, nationalism was once seen as linked to anti-India sentiment. But that era is over now.' He asked Finance Minister Wagle what era he was talking about. Gyawali, who is also a former foreign minister, has commented that Wagle's statement is undiplomatic, irrelevant, and damaging to Nepal's self-respect and interests. His answer is that there has never been an 'era of anti-India nationalism' in Nepal. Gyawali's statement is as follows, Finance Minister Dr. Swarnim Wagle's statement in New Delhi that 'the era of anti-India nationalism in Nepal is over' is undiplomatic, irrelevant and detrimental to Nepal's self-respect and interests. Foreign soil is not the place for any government official to discuss the internal political differences of their country. There was never an 'era of anti-India nationalism' in Nepal. Nepal has always wanted and still wants friendly relations based on sovereign equality and mutual benefit and respect. The view held by any particular individual or group is not an 'era' in itself. Nor does it represent the nation as a whole. What 'era' is the Finance Minister talking about? There are several problems between Nepal and India. The border issue, some provisions of the 1950 treaty that give the impression of a security umbrella, the hassle that Nepali products have to face to enter the Indian market due to the liberal trade policy, the increasing trade deficit, the annual flooding of Nepali land due to the one-way dams built on the border, the reluctance to provide Nepal with an alternative air entry route that is natural to it, etc. It is important to have open discussions about these issues with close neighbors and friends. Hiding problems under the rug will not strengthen relationships. Raising these issues is not against any particular country. This is a question of Nepal's national interest. It is the responsibility of every government to protect this national interest. The only way to find a solution is to build strong national unity and consensus on these issues, backed by serious diplomatic initiatives. A policy of appeasement that covers up the reality does not strengthen national interests and self-respect, but rather undermines them.

CPN-UML leader Pradeep Gyawali has objected to the statement made by Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle. Speaking at the NDTV World Summit 2026 held in New Delhi, Finance Minister Wagle said that the era of nationalism linked to anti-India sentiment in Nepal is over. He had said, 'In Nepal, nationalism was once seen as linked to anti-India sentiment. But that era is over now.' He asked Finance Minister Wagle what era he was talking about. Gyawali, who is also a former foreign minister, has commented that Wagle's statement is undiplomatic, irrelevant, and damaging to Nepal's self-respect and interests. His answer is that there has never been an 'era of anti-India nationalism' in Nepal. Gyawali's statement is as follows, Finance Minister Dr. Swarnim Wagle's statement in New Delhi that 'the era of anti-India nationalism in Nepal is over' is undiplomatic, irrelevant and detrimental to Nepal's self-respect and interests. Foreign soil is not the place for any government official to discuss the internal political differences of their country. There was never an 'era of anti-India nationalism' in Nepal. Nepal has always wanted and still wants friendly relations based on sovereign equality and mutual benefit and respect. The view held by any particular individual or group is not an 'era' in itself. Nor does it represent the nation as a whole. What 'era' is the Finance Minister talking about? There are several problems between Nepal and India. The border issue, some provisions of the 1950 treaty that give the impression of a security umbrella, the hassle that Nepali products have to face to enter the Indian market due to the liberal trade policy, the increasing trade deficit, the annual flooding of Nepali land due to the one-way dams built on the border, the reluctance to provide Nepal with an alternative air entry route that is natural to it, etc. It is important to have open discussions about these issues with close neighbors and friends. Hiding problems under the rug will not strengthen relationships. Raising these issues is not against any particular country. This is a question of Nepal's national interest. It is the responsibility of every government to protect this national interest. The only way to find a solution is to build strong national unity and consensus on these issues, backed by serious diplomatic initiatives. A policy of appeasement that covers up the reality does not strengthen national interests and self-respect, but rather undermines them.
